speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are having difficulties conceiving and experiencing discomfort during sexual activity; to help you, I need to start by asking: Are you or your partner currently undergoing any fertility treatments, and have you noticed any specific triggers for the pain, such as penetration or deep thrusting?

speaker: Patient
text: 30-year-old female. The patient and her husband have been trying to conceive for 15 months without success. They are sexually active at least twice a week. The husband occasionally has difficulties maintaining an erection. The patient reports discomfort and pelvic floor muscle tension during attempted vaginal penetration. Diagnosed with body dysmorphic disorder three years ago. No family history of serious illness. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. No medications.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Dyspareunia secondary to pelvic floor muscle tension (vaginismus) with concurrent male erectile dysfunction contributing to conception difficulties.

The patient's history of body dysmorphic disorder may also contribute to anxiety-related pelvic guarding. Given the 15-month duration of trying to conceive without success, I will request a full fertility workup including a semen analysis for the husband and ovarian reserve testing for the patient, alongside a referral to a pelvic floor physical therapist.
